note: The pattern language, independent of any design system. Every entry is one recurring user intent at one scale, resolved to a variant by forces. Profiles realize variants and parts in their own patterns/index.json and never add abstract patterns of their own. The schema is deliberately small: only fields the generator (engine/scripts/patterns-doc.ts) reads are here, because unread fields are the ones that grow. `resolve` is an ordered list; the first rule whose every listed force equals the declared value wins. A `redirect` rule that consults an undeclared force asks for it; a `variant` rule that does is skipped. Registration: a new abstract pattern must occupy an (intent, scale) cell nothing else does, or differ from its nearest neighbour on a named force; a new variant must be selected by a `when` no sibling already matches; anything else is a realization and belongs in a profile. See docs/patterns-v2.md.

intents.choose: Pick from options the system already knows.
intents.enter: Supply a value the system does not have.
intents.act: Invoke a command that changes something.
intents.confirm: Consent to a consequence before it happens.
intents.navigate: Move between views, or learn where you are.
intents.report: Be told what happened, or what state things are in.
intents.group: See related things as one thing.

scales.region: A named area of a screen.

represents.about: What an option or control stands for. Decides choose vs act vs navigate before anything else does.

judge.question: What does that control stand for to the person using it?

criteria.value: It picks or sets a value the system already knows about — an option, a setting, a piece of data. Using it changes what some value is, not where the user is. A select, a checkbox-style menu item, a colour swatch, or a disclosure button whose visible label is the value it will change all count.
criteria.command: It invokes a command that changes something — save, delete, duplicate, upload, undo, retry, close, or opening a dialog or panel to do one of those. Using it does something rather than going somewhere or setting a value.
criteria.destination: It moves the user to another view, screen, route, record or URL. Using it changes where the user is, however the control happens to be styled — a button that routes is still a destination.
criteria.none: Not an interactive control at all: static text or a display-only element that happens to use a control component.

multiplicity.about: How many options may be chosen at once.

cardinality.about: Size of a set: few is 2–5, some is 6–15, many is more than 15. Used for options, fields, actions and views alike.

set.about: Whether the user can supply something the system does not list.

representation.about: Whether a value or option has a visual identity. If it does, show it: a name is a description of the choice, not the choice.

fit.about: Whether the whole set sits on one line at rest.

value-type.about: The type of a value the user enters.

optionality.about: Optional means unset until the user sets it: it inherits a default and can be reset to it.

binding.about: Whether a form's fields are local state or a record the store owns and saves.

context.about: Where an interaction happens relative to the thing it concerns.

relation.about: How views relate: peers of one subject, or levels of one hierarchy.

grouped.about: Whether items fall into named groups that mean something.

prominence.about: How much attention an action deserves. At most one primary per surface.

reversibility.about: Whether the user can undo the action afterwards.

persistence.about: For messages: goes away on its own, or stays until dealt with.

subject.about: For messages: what is being reported.

selection.about: For collections: whether items are selectable, and whether one selection drives something else.

boundary.about: For groups: whether the grouping needs a visible box or just rhythm.

series.about: For groups: whether the content is a run of like items — points, steps, entries — rather than one piece.

structure.about: What a region edits: one thing's own fields, or several things and the connections between them.

placement.about: Whether where something sits is computed from the data every time, or put there by the author and kept.

containers.note: Containers are not patterns. A pattern declares `context` and the profile maps the container. The decision that used to live in authoring.md's Modal/Dialog/AlertDialog/Drawer paragraph lives here.
containers.region: A persistent area within a screen: main, aside, header.
containers.modal: Blocks the parent view until dismissed. For a focused, single-decision task the user can scan without scrolling, reachable from more than one entry point.
containers.drawer: Slides over the parent view and keeps it visible. For editing something already on screen, or a multi-section task a modal would cramp.
containers.popover: Anchored to its trigger, non-modal, small. For a control that expands in place.
containers.menu: A popover of items: commands, destinations, or settings scoped to the thing the trigger sits on.

patterns.problem: The user picks from a set of options the system already knows.

parts.note: Each option is either its name or its rendering.
The chosen option is visible at rest.

resolve.because: A list of things to do is a menu, not a choice of value.
A list of places to go is navigation.

segmented.summary: All options visible on one row, the active one marked; re-selecting the active one clears it when 'no opinion' is a valid state.
segmented.consequences: Costs width. Buys zero clicks to see the set — a dropdown for four icons costs a click and a popover to say what four icons say at rest.

radio.summary: All options visible as a labelled vertical list.
radio.consequences: Costs height. Right when the labels are too long for a row.

select.summary: The current value is the trigger; the set opens on demand.
select.consequences: Costs a click to see the options. Buys space. The default, not the reflex.

combobox.summary: Typed filtering over a long set; the value is one of its options.
combobox.consequences: Justified only when the set is too long to scan. A typed value the set lacks is not a value here; where it should stand, that is autocomplete.

autocomplete.summary: A text input that suggests known values as the user types; what was typed stands even when nothing matches.
autocomplete.consequences: Right only when the set is open. Where the value has to be one of the options, an unmatched entry gets through here and fails later; that is combobox.

rendered.summary: The option is its rendering — a swatch, a word set in its face, a live preview — laid out as a grid of tiles with the active one marked; the name is secondary, in a tooltip or caption.
rendered.consequences: The only correct answer when options differ visibly. A dropdown of their names describes the choice instead of showing it.

checklist.summary: Every option visible with an independent on/off.

token-list.summary: Chosen options shown as removable tokens; unchosen ones found by typing.

patterns.problem: The user supplies a value of a known type that the system cannot list in advance.

parts.note: A rendered value type shows the value, not its name.

resolve.because: A value from a fixed set is a choice.

text.summary: A single- or multi-line text input.

number.summary: A numeric input; a slider beside it when the range is bounded and feel matters more than the exact figure.

length.summary: A CSS length: a unit-aware input and a slider under one label, the slider's range derived from the unit.
length.consequences: One hardcoded range is wrong for one of the two unit families. A text field holding '16px' is this pattern missing.

color.summary: The current color shown as itself; the editor opens on demand; reset appears only while a local value is set.
color.consequences: An always-open picker per slot is a wall of pickers. An always-present reset on an inherited value lies about what it would do.

media.summary: Pick or upload; the current asset shown as itself.

date.summary: A calendar, or a typed date with the format shown.

patterns.problem: A control needs a label the accessibility tree can find, a description, and somewhere for its validation message.

field.summary: Label, control, description and error in the standard arrangement, with the associations wired.
field.consequences: A placeholder is not a label. A label beside a control with no association is a picture of a field.

patterns.problem: Several fields belong together under one heading, and some of them may not apply until the user says so.

parts.note: Per field, and for the group.

fieldset.summary: A legend and its fields, all shown.

collapsible.summary: A heading that opens to its fields; closed by default when the group is auxiliary.

progressive.summary: Only fields that hold a value, or are shown by default, render; each has its own reset and the group has reset-all.
progressive.consequences: Twelve possible controls show as three. Every unconditionally rendered optional control is one the reader has to rule out. A hand-rolled 'Show advanced' toggle hides half of them and resets none.

patterns.problem: The user edits the fields of one thing and the result is saved or discarded.

parts.note: Absent when binding is entity and every edit is saved as it happens.

data-form.summary: Fields declared as data and rendered by the system's form renderer against the record store: no local state, no save button, undo for free.
data-form.consequences: The one form variant whose anti-shape is checkable — an overlay or card holding bare text controls with a state hook per field.

dialog.summary: A modal with the fields and a submit/cancel cluster in the standard place.
dialog.consequences: Right when the task is one decision the user can scan without scrolling.

drawer.summary: A side surface for a multi-section edit that keeps the subject visible.

inspector.summary: A persistent aside that edits whatever is selected in the main region, with its own header and scroll area.

patterns.problem: The user builds several things and the connections between them, and it is the connections that have to be read and changed.

parts.note: One card per thing, carrying what the reader needs at a glance. Its fields are edited elsewhere (edit-record.inspector), so the card holds no controls of its own.
The connections. The region routes them — where a line leaves and arrives is a decision about every other line, not one the author makes.
Optional: stretches of the canvas whose boundaries give a position meaning, so moving a card across one changes what that thing is.

The verbs that need no second thing to name them: add one here, delete this, lay it out again. A verb that needs one — where a connection goes — belongs in the inspector, against the read-out of the same setting.

resolve.because: One thing's own fields are a form, however the region draws them.

canvas.summary: The author arranges the things and draws the connections: positions are theirs and are kept, and the layout only re-runs when asked for.
canvas.consequences: Every gesture has to say what it will do while it is still held, because a drop that silently does nothing is the failure this variant invites. A layout that re-runs on any edit undoes the arrangement the author just made.

auto-layout.summary: The structure is edited and the layout is computed from it every time, so there is nothing to arrange and nothing to reset.
auto-layout.consequences: Right while the shape is small or forced by the data; wrong the moment the author has a reason to put two things side by side, because nothing can keep it.

patterns.problem: More than one command applies here and they must read as a set with one obvious default.

parts.note: At most one per surface, positioned last.
Secondary and destructive commands that do not earn a visible button.

resolve.because: Something that navigates is a link, however it is styled.

bar.summary: Two or three visible actions, consistently ordered, gap-spaced, primary last.
bar.consequences: Too small to check by shape; it is the documented default. A div with hand-set margins between the buttons is this pattern missing.

toolbar.summary: Grouped commands with one tab stop and arrow-key movement between them.
toolbar.consequences: A stack of buttons with a separator looks identical and makes every control a tab stop.

overflow.summary: Secondary and destructive commands behind one icon-triggered menu. Items that would do nothing are omitted, not disabled. A destructive item opens confirm and never destroys on its own.
overflow.consequences: Rename and Delete as two visible buttons compete with the one action that matters.

patterns.problem: An action cannot be undone and the user must consent to it knowingly.

parts.note: Names the consequence, not the button.
Exactly two: the consequence labelled as its verb, and cancel. Emphasis matches severity.

resolve.because: Reversible actions get an undo, not a question. A confirm on a reversible action trains the user to click through it.

confirm.summary: A modal that blocks until the user chooses; dismissing is cancel.
confirm.consequences: A form dialog also has a title, a description and two buttons, and tree matching cannot tell the two apart. The declaration can.

patterns.problem: Content is nested deeper than one level, and showing it all at once makes a wall.

parts.note: One route per screen, declared flat. The path is the state, so a router can drive it and deep links work.

A row that names the sub-screen and opens it: one control, one tab stop, one accessible name. A trailing chevron means 'goes deeper'; a trailing value means 'this is the current setting'; never both. When representation is rendered, the row's leading element is the value itself — five swatches, the family name in its own face — not a label for it.
Back, title, optional description, state controls on the right. No breadcrumb one level deep.
Shows only what is actually set.

resolve.because: Tabs are for peers; depth wants navigation.

drilldown.summary: A stack of screens navigated one level at a time; rows descend, headers ascend.
drilldown.consequences: Depth beats breadth: twelve settings behind four rows is a menu; twelve on one screen is a wall. A select that swaps which panel renders, and tabs standing in for levels, are both this pattern refused.

patterns.problem: One subject has several peer views and only one should show at a time.

parts.note: One per tab. A panel may itself hold a navigate-hierarchy; the outer footer stays put.

tabs.summary: A tab list and one panel per tab, sharing whatever surrounds them.
tabs.consequences: A select that swaps the body is a tab bar that costs a click and hides the alternatives. Several overlays for one task with several sources is this pattern inside one overlay.

patterns.problem: The user moves between the top-level sections of an app or site from anywhere in it, and must be able to tell which section they are in.

parts.note: One link per section, each to its own route; the section the user is in is marked current to assistive technology, not by colour alone.
A named set of sections behind one trigger, which opens a panel of their links.

list.summary: Every section as one link in one list — a row in a top bar or a column at the side — with the current one marked.
list.consequences: One list, laid out for the width it has: a second navigation built for small screens disagrees with the first the day a section is added.

panels.summary: Sections in named groups; each group's trigger opens a panel of its links, and choosing one closes it.
panels.consequences: Costs a click or a hover to see a group. Right when the sections are too many for one list, or a link needs a line of description before anyone can choose it.

patterns.problem: Many items of one kind must be found, compared and acted on.

parts.note: Search, one choose per filter dimension, bulk actions — one row above the items. Announce the result count when a filter changes.

resolve.because: A grid of previews where one is picked is a choice, not a browse.

list.summary: The system's data view: fields declared as data; sorting, filtering and pagination owned by the view.
list.consequences: A hand-built table with its own filter row is this pattern reimplemented. A list long enough to need filtering that offers none is this pattern missing a part.

selectable-list.summary: A listbox where one item is selected and the selection drives a preview elsewhere; one tab stop for the list, arrows within it.
selectable-list.consequences: A stack of buttons with hand-managed aria-selected has the look and none of the semantics.

gallery.summary: Grouped, live-rendered items as the reference — not screenshots, not names — with real group semantics; previews are inert.
gallery.consequences: Sections built from headings alone group visually and not semantically.

grouped-list.summary: Items sectioned by an attribute that decides what may be done to them, each section with its own add and overflow, each row descending to its own editor.
grouped-list.consequences: Editing happens on the item's own screen, not inline in the row. One flat list hides the attribute that governs the actions.

patterns.problem: Some content is wanted only some of the time, and shown at rest it crowds out what is wanted every time.

parts.note: The control that shows and hides the panel: it names what the panel holds and says whether it is open.
What the trigger reveals. Nothing in it is needed to make sense of the rest of the view.

resolve.because: Content big enough for a screen of its own is a level to descend to, not a panel to unfold.

collapsible.summary: One panel shown and hidden in place by the control that names it; what follows moves to make room.
collapsible.consequences: Costs a click to see what is inside, so nothing the task needs belongs there. A heading with a click handler over a hidden div looks the same and tells assistive technology nothing.

accordion.summary: Several named sections, each heading the trigger for its own panel, opened in place.
accordion.consequences: An accordion of one section is a collapsible with an accordion's markup.

anchored.summary: The panel opens over the view, anchored to its trigger and non-modal; moving on closes it.
anchored.consequences: Small, and about the control that opened it. Anything the user has to scroll inside, or must finish before going on, belongs in a dialog or a drawer.

patterns.problem: The system has something to tell the user about what happened or what state things are in.

parts.note: Undo, retry, dismiss, or the action that fills an empty region.

toast.summary: Transient, raised from anywhere, queued and dismissed by a manager the app mounts once; carries undo when the action was reversible.
toast.consequences: A hand-managed array of messages in state, rendered into a fixed stack, is the manager reimplemented.

notice.summary: Persistent and region-level, stacked by one container that owns order, spacing and dismissal.
notice.consequences: Individually placed notices with local margins disagree about spacing and never agree about order.

inline.summary: Beside the field it concerns, in the field's own error slot.

empty.summary: Why the region is empty and the action that fills it, centred in the space the content would occupy.
empty.consequences: A bare 'No results' string, or a spinner that never resolves, are both this pattern missing.

loading.summary: A placeholder shaped like the content, or a spinner when the shape is unknown.

patterns.problem: Related content and its actions should read as one thing.

card.summary: A bounded surface with an optional header, title and actions.
card.consequences: A styled div with a border rebuilt per surface disagrees with itself about radius, padding and header rhythm.

section.summary: A heading and its content, rhythm from the parent, no box.

list.summary: Like items in a run, bulleted, or numbered when their order means something; the list spaces them, not each item.
list.consequences: Lines that start with a typed bullet or number look like a list and are not one to assistive technology: no count, and no way to skip past it.

patterns.problem: Every view must tell the user where they are and what they can do here before it shows them anything else.

parts.note: Title, optional breadcrumbs or icon, optional description, trailing actions. Rebuilt per screen is the defect.

page.summary: A root screen: header, main, optional aside.

sub-screen.summary: A screen below the root of a hierarchy; its header is navigate-hierarchy#sub-screen-header.

overlay.summary: A screen hosted in a modal or drawer: the container supplies header and footer, the body may be a switch-view.
